title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Ta

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (5) states \((x_1-x_t)/(1-t)=(x_1-x_0)/(1-t)\). Given \(x_t=(1-t)x_0+t x_1\), the correct identity is \((x_1-x_t)/(1-t)=x_1-x_0\), with no remaining \(1-t\) denominator. As written, Eq. (5) defines a different, incorrectly time-rescaled target. This also contradicts Algorithm 1 and later text, which correctly use \(u^{\mathrm{cond}}=x_1-x_0\).

The numerator integral retains a prefactor \(1/n\) in Eqs. (27) and (28), but Eq. (29) drops that prefactor. The correct Eq. (29) should be \((1/n)\sum_i \cdots\). Since the denominator in Eq. (26) also contains \(1/n\), the factors cancel only if both are retained. As written, taking the ratio of Eqs. (24)/(26) and (29) would introduce an erroneous factor of \(n\), so the displayed derivation does not prove Proposition 1.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.3, proof of Proposition 2(iii), Equations (70)–(74)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: There is a missing factor of \(n\). From Eq. (70), \(n/M\,\mathbb E[\sum_{j=1}^M w^{(i_j)}(u^{(i_j)})^2]\) equals \(n\,\mathbb E_{i\sim\mathrm{Unif}}[w^{(i)}u^{(i)2}]\), not the unscaled expectation in Eq. (71). The same missing factor is then implicitly ignored when Eq. (72) is identified with the posterior-weighted second moment in Eq. (73). Thus the variance proof as written is invalid. In addition, the proof uses scalar squares although the velocity is vector-valued, whereas the stated \(\operatorname{Var}\) inequality would require a specified scalarization or covariance-matrix ordering.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1 versus the paragraph immediately following Proposition 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly asserts exact unbiasedness: Proposition 2(ii) states \(\mathbb E[\hat u_M^\star]=\hat u^\star\), and Appendix B.1 says reuse of \(b^{(1)}\) 'yields an unbiased estimator.' Immediately after Proposition 2, however, the manuscript says that inclusion of \(b^{(1)}\) 'does not guarantee unbiasedness in the standard Monte Carlo sense' and that the claims 'therefore approximate unbiasedness within empirical tolerance.' These are mutually incompatible descriptions of the same estimator and theorem.

The paper infers posterior/softmax collapse from cosine alignment: 'this corresponds to a collapse towards 0 of all but one of the softmax weights.' That implication is false. A weighted average of multiple conditional velocity vectors can have cosine similarity near one with one selected target when the vectors are correlated or approximately collinear; cosine similarity also discards magnitude differences. The reported diagnostic therefore does not establish that the target is effectively deterministic, that one posterior weight dominates, or that stochastic target variation is negligible. Direct weight concentration/entropy and target-error or variance measurements would be required for the claimed conclusion.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, paragraph beginning 'Figure 2 confirms that generalization arises...'; Contributions and Abstract
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The manuscript says Figure 2 'confirms that generalization arises when the network fails to estimate' \(\hat u^\star\). Yet the same paragraph explicitly concedes that, for the larger datasets allegedly exhibiting generalization, the increase in nearest-training-image distance is 'modest and within margin of error,' providing 'only weak evidence that the model generalizes better'; error bars are omitted. The reported correlation between dataset size, approximation error, and FID therefore cannot support the causal and definitive wording 'generalization arises when' or the abstract's claim to rule out a key explanation.

Appendix C says it presents 'the results for the MNIST dataset,' but both Table 1 and Table 2 are captioned 'FID FMNIST.' The text additionally discusses separate classifier accuracies for MNIST and FMNIST, while neither table unambiguously identifies its dataset beyond the duplicated FMNIST caption. Consequently, the dataset associated with at least one table is misreported or the claimed MNIST results are absent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph discussing the memorization/generalization phase transition
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites 'Zhang et al. (2024, unpublished)' as support for a phase transition. The reference list, however, gives Zhang et al., 'The emergence of reproducibility and consistency in diffusion models,' 'In ICML, 2024,' i.e. a published conference paper. The publication status is incorrectly reported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix D.5, experimental details for Figure 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 4 reports CIFAR-10 and CelebA-64 comparisons. Appendix D.5 says its CIFAR protocol is for 'Figures 2 and 3' and its CelebA protocol is for 'Figure 3'; it does not actually state the Figure 4 training protocol despite claiming to provide Figure 4 details. This is not merely a cross-reference typo: Figure 4 compares several methods and target sample sizes, for which training duration, architecture, and protocol are necessary to interpret the result. The setup description is internally mismatched and incomplete.
